delete.summary:
Drop the lease, decrement the slot's refcount. When the refcount
reaches zero the slot is eligible for the producer's next
AcquireRingSlot. Idempotent: releasing an already-released lease
is a no-op.

post.summary:
Reserve the next available slot in `ring_id`. PM picks the slot
(round-robin over slots whose refcount has hit zero since they
were last committed); the returned (slot_idx, generation) is the
triple the producer will write into the downstream event's
RingSlotRef.
post.description:
Fails with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED when no slot is available (every
slot is currently leased by at least one consumer) and the ring's
exhaustion_policy is DROP_NEW. With BLOCK the call waits.

post.summary:
Publish the just-written slot. PM marks the slot ready-for-lease
so consumers' LeaseRingSlot calls succeed. The producer publishes
the downstream domain event (e.g. RadioCaptureEvent) on NATS
carrying the RingSlotRef in parallel; consumers see the event
and call LeaseRingSlot to take the read lease.
post.description:
Fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION if (slot_idx, generation) doesn't
match the producer's last AcquireRingSlot — guards against
double-commit or commits on stale handles.

get.summary:
One-time discovery on consumer startup. Returns the ring's slot
count + per-slot shm names so the consumer can mmap (and, for GPU
consumers, cudaHostRegister + cudaHostGetDevicePointer) every
slot ahead of the hot path. The returned shm names are stable
for the lifetime of the PM process; clients should not poll
MapRing per-capture.
get.description:
Fails with NOT_FOUND if the ring isn't configured in PM's static
config.

post.summary:
Bump the slot's refcount and grant a read lease. Lightweight —
no bytes cross the wire, only the (ring_id, slot_idx, generation)
triple and the returned opaque lease_id.
post.description:
Fails with FAILED_PRECONDITION if the generation no longer matches
the slot's current generation (consumer was too slow, producer
already recycled the slot). The consumer should skip this capture
and wait for the next event.

sizeBytes.description:
How many bytes of capacity were actually written. Surfaces into
RingSlotRef.size_bytes for downstream consumers.

generation.description:
The generation the consumer expects to read. Comes from the
RingSlotRef carried in the upstream event. PM rejects with
FAILED_PRECONDITION if the slot has since advanced.

slotIdx.description:
The reservation. Producer fills the slot up to size_bytes_written
(≤ capacity_bytes), then calls CommitRingSlot with (slot_idx,
generation, size_bytes_written). The generation here is the one
assigned to this acquire — bumps from the slot's previous use.

shmName.description:
POSIX shm name for this slot. Producer mmaps + writes; PM does not
copy any bytes through gRPC. Names are stable across the slot's
lifetime — a producer that holds onto its mmap across calls can
reuse it.

capacityBytes.description: Slot capacity in bytes. Set at ring creation time; immutable.

committedAt.description:
Server-assigned timestamp the commit landed. Useful for end-to-end
latency measurement vs the event's capture_time_ns.

leaseId.description:
Opaque handle the consumer passes back to ReleaseRingSlot. Carries
server-side bookkeeping (which slot, which generation, when the
lease was granted) — opaque to the client.

slotIdx.description: For diagnostics / metrics. Matches the request fields.

nSlots.description:
N — the number of pre-allocated slots in this ring. Consumer
builds an N-entry pointer array on startup.

slotCapacityBytes.description: Per-slot capacity. Same for every slot in a ring.

slotShmNames.description:
POSIX shm name per slot, indexed by slot_idx. The consumer
shm_open + mmap each name, then (for GPU consumers)
cudaHostRegister + cudaHostGetDevicePointer to build the
per-slot device-pointer cache.

backingTier.description:
Implementation hint: how the producer's slots get filled. CPU
producers mmap the same shm; GPU producers would also need a
matching cudaHostRegister. Surfaced so consumers can sanity-check
(e.g., a GPU consumer paired with a CPU producer is the common
case and works; the reverse needs the GPU-producer probe to pass).

v1Tier.description:
Ordered from fastest → most durable.
Higher tiers may not always be available.

 - TIER_UNSPECIFIED: Not set; treated as an error in most contexts.
 - TIER_GPU: GPU device memory (fastest, smallest, most volatile).
 - TIER_RAM: Host DRAM / shared-memory segment.
 - TIER_DISK_HOT: Primary local durable level (NVMe/SSD; durable, larger,
 - TIER_OBJECT: slower than RAM). See TIER_DISK_COLD for the optional
slower second local level.

Remote object storage (S3/GCS/Azure; durable, largest).
 - TIER_VOID: Discard on eviction: payload is deleted rather than moved.
 - TIER_RAM_RING: Pre-allocated /dev/shm ring of N fixed slots, rotated across
 - TIER_DISK_COLD: captures. Producers acquire a slot, write, commit; consumers
map the ring once at startup (no per-capture mmap or
cudaHostRegister) and lease the indicated slot per cycle.
See payload/manager/services/v1/payload_ring_service.proto.
